numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For an indefinite P with assume_PSD=True (both M1 and M2 non-empty), the second if-block unconditionally overwrote expr with the M2 (negative-eigenvalue) term, silently discarding the positive-eigenvalue M1 term. The solver then minimized only the negative-eigenvalue part (-scale * ||M2^T x||^2), producing a wrong canonical form and a wrong optimal value with status=OPTIMAL and no exception. For P=diag(2,-1) and x=[1,2], the pre-fix code returned -4 with status OPTIMAL where the true x^T P x = -2.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: For indefinite P, quad_form canonicalization should raise ValueError rather than silently produce incorrect results. The error message should include 'indefinite' and 'PSD'.

the DCP check does not catch this case when assume_PSD=True (the issue only arises with assume_PSD=True)

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Tiny negative eigenvalues on the order of 1e-14 from floating-point construction (e.g., A^T A or covariance matrices) are cited as a trigger; the wrong-value example uses small integers (P=diag(2,-1), x=[1,2]).
category_specific_evidence: The violated property is the quadratic form identity: for P=diag(2,-1) and x=[1,2], the true x^T P x = -2, but the pre-fix code returned -4 with status OPTIMAL.

The bug arises because quad_form_canon overwrote the M1 (positive-eigenvalue) sum_squares expression with the M2 (negative-eigenvalue) expression, so only -scale*||M2^T x||^2 reached quad_over_lin_canon.
The bug was reported as affecting cp.quad_form(x, P, assume_PSD=True) and was fixed in quad_form_canon by raising ValueError for indefinite P.
The regression test test_indefinite_assume_psd_raises solves with prob.solve(solver=cp.SCS, use_quad_obj=False) and expects a ValueError whose message contains 'indefinite' and 'PSD'.
The fix's ValueError message suggests symmetrizing P and clipping negative eigenvalues when P is intended to be PSD.
reproduction_risks: Reproduction must use use_quad_obj=False so the conic path calling quad_form_canon is taken; the QP path used by SCS >= 3.0 bypasses it.
Without assume_PSD=True the DCP check catches indefinite P, so the bug only reproduces with assume_PSD=True.
The bug was described in CVXPY 1.8.1 and earlier; later versions contain the fix and will raise ValueError instead of returning a value.
Matrices with ~1e-14 negative eigenvalues from floating-point error may now hit the new ValueError rather than being silently handled.
